which_results_affected: None. The paper never cites the FK paper. Its only OpenAI input is a different preprint, "Cardy's formula for critical Poisson–Voronoi percolation" (Sept 23 2026). That preprint mentions the FK paper only as related work and says outright that it does not use it. Theorem thm:main and everything downstream (Prop. quenched-cardy, Lemma chart-cardy, the exploration, test and sewing sections) keep their proofs as far as this gap is concerned.
evidence:
1. No direct citation. The paper's own bibliography (build/references.tex) has no entry for "Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1<=q<4". It has no random-cluster, FK or square-lattice-interface reference at all. Its only OpenAI reference is:
  \bibitem{supplied-cardy} OpenAI, \emph{Cardy's formula for critical Poisson--Voronoi percolation} ... OAI:Cardys-formula-for-critical-Poisson-Voronoi-percolation-September-23-2026
A full list of every \cite in the sections and paper.tex shows no FK key.

2. How it uses that other OpenAI paper (01-introduction.tex): "Our input is the scalar annealed Cardy conclusion of the companion manuscript~\cite[Theorem~1.1]{supplied-cardy}." It is packaged as Hypothesis hyp:cardy ("Scalar critical Cardy formula ... annealed probability of C_Q in fair-colored full-plane Poisson--Voronoi percolation converges ... to F(x)"), with the line "This is the conclusion of \cite[Theorem~1.1]{supplied-cardy} at precisely its scalar, geometry-averaged scope." Theorem thm:main is stated as "Assume Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:cardy}." The Cardy formula it depends on is the Voronoi one, not the square-lattice FK one.

3. Indirect path checked. The Voronoi Cardy preprint (Cardys-formula-for-critical-Poisson-Voronoi-percolation-September-23-2026/build) cites the FK paper as OpenAISquareBond2026, note "Theorem~1.2". It does so in one place only, sections/00-introduction.tex:80-86: "The same Cardy function is obtained for critical square-lattice bond percolation under uniform marked-Jordan approximation \cite[Theorem~1.2]{OpenAISquareBond2026}. ... The square-bond theorem is not used in our proof." Searching all of its sources for that key turns up nothing else. So the chain through Sec. 7.3 / Theorem hol:disk / Theorem intro:main / the FK Cardy theorem never reaches this paper's results.

Caveat: this answer covers only the FK gap you described. I did not check whether the Voronoi Cardy Theorem 1.1 is itself sound. This paper's main theorem is conditional on it either way.
